items.title: A randomized-and-derandomized subprocedure that finds a large vertex set meeting every edge of a 2-3-uniform hypergraph in the required parity
items.author: Johan H{\aa}stad, Bj\"orn Martinsson, Tamio-Vesa Nakajima, Stanislav \v{Z}ivn\'y
authors: Johan H{\aa}stad, Bj\"orn Martinsson, Tamio-Vesa Nakajima, Stanislav \v{Z}ivn\'y
items.work: A logarithmic approximation of linearly ordered colourings
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the subprocedure lemma of the paper (author lemma at source lines 151-156, label lem:innerstep): for a {2,3}-uniform hypergraph that admits an LO 2-colouring and whose system Av = 1^m fixes no variable, produce a vertex set T of size at least n/2 that meets every 3-edge in zero or two vertices and every 2-edge in exactly one vertex, in O(n^3 + nm) time. The proof (source lines 158-182) is not a routine greedy step: it first reads the solution set of the linear system as an affine space and chooses a random solution to make the membership of each vertex in T a fair coin, with the odd-parity condition on every edge following from the parity of the right-hand side (proof lines 159-167), and then converts the randomised guarantee into a deterministic one by the method of conditional expectations, fixing the variables a_i one at a time so that at least half of the coordinates determined at that step become zero (proof lines 169-180). The bound |T| >= n/2 is exactly what the main algorithm needs from the subprocedure. H2.
